## Notifiers roadmap

---
status: active
type: roadmap
owner: notifiers
---

## Priority execution plan — current develop direction (2026-11-08)

> Current assessment: no critical defect was established in the audited notifier package. Telegram transport, bounded serialized delivery, credential redaction, failure isolation and Harvester integration are already implemented.

### IMPORTANT — preserve safe best-effort notification behavior

- [x] **Consumer-selectable Telegram event subscriptions — [#996](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/996).** Keep profile resolution in consuming applications. The Notifiers package exposes a validated per-subscriber event-name subset and bounded formatters for additional operational messages; omitting the selection preserves the existing full-allowlist behavior.

1. **Keep Harvester's Telegram integration aligned with the notifier contract.**
   - **Why:** operational alerts are useful only if they remain high-signal and cannot affect order processing, accounting, recovery or shutdown.
   - **Do:** mark the Harvester integration complete (PR #734); maintain the fixed supported-event allowlist, validated per-subscriber event selection, bounded queue, Harvester-owned policy/credential configuration, and isolated setup/delivery failures. Keep formatting and transport code inside this package.
   - **Verify:** retain offline integration tests for startup with notifications disabled, partial credentials, setup failure, malformed events, queue saturation, transport failure and orderly shutdown.

2. **Perform the operator-controlled Telegram smoke test when a dedicated test chat is available.**
   - **Why:** fake-fetch tests prove request handling but do not prove the operator's bot token/chat configuration or real Telegram API acceptance.
   - **Do:** use the existing one-message, credential-gated smoke-test command with a dedicated test chat. Do not put credentials in source, logs or PR output and do not add the smoke test to default CI.
   - **Verify:** record only timestamp, command exit/result and redacted API acceptance; do not retry ambiguous delivery automatically.

### DEFERRED — only when a real consumer requires it

3. **Do not add automatic retries, email/Discord providers or a persistent outbox by default.**
   - **Why:** ambiguous network outcomes can duplicate messages; extra transports/outbox infrastructure create new operational ownership and dependencies.
   - **Do:** require a concrete consumer, duplicate-send/idempotency policy, rate-limit contract and storage owner before implementation.
   - **Verify:** each future provider receives isolated tests, coverage and explicit shutdown/error guarantees. Keep the package dependency-free where practical.

**Owner:** packages/notifiers/
**Status:** Telegram transport, provider-oriented source layout, reliability hardening, real EventBus integration coverage, delivery diagnostics, Node 22/24 CI, and operator-controlled smoke-test tooling are merged into develop (PRs #346, #348, #356, #360, and Harvester integration PR #734). The validation-hardening audit was completed in PR #379; the live Telegram smoke test remains an operator-only action.
**Purpose:** provide small, dependency-free notification transports for operational alerts from Coinzilla applications.

Read AGENTS.md, README.md, and the repository's mandatory AI_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md.

## Product goals

1. Deliver high-signal operational events without coupling notification I/O to trading execution.
2. Keep the package dependency-free by preferring Node.js built-ins and injected side-effect boundaries.
3. Keep each transport isolated under its own folder, with a thin package entry point.
4. Make outbound content safe through explicit event allowlists and curated formatters.
5. Make delivery ordering, admission limits, failure handling, timeouts, and shutdown behavior explicit and testable.
6. Add transports only when a concrete consumer needs them; avoid speculative frameworks and empty provider scaffolding.

## Target architecture

    packages/notifiers/
      src/
        index.js                 # stable package exports only
        telegram/                # implemented feature module
          event-subscriber.js     # event-bus subscription and delivery lifecycle
          notifier.js             # Telegram HTTP transport
          index.js                 # provider-local public exports
          notifier.test.js
          event-subscriber.test.js
          helpers/                 # pure supporting functions only
            validate-telegram-inputs.js
            validate-telegram-api-response.js
            sanitize-error-message.js
        email/                    # future; create when implemented
        discord/                  # future; create when implemented

Each provider owns its transport client, provider-specific formatter, event integration where applicable, and tests. Keep cross-provider abstractions out until at least two implemented providers demonstrate a real shared contract.

## Phase 0 — Package foundation

- [x] Create the private pnpm workspace package @coinzilla/notifiers.
- [x] Define a thin public entry point and package-local AI-agent instructions.
- [x] Keep the initial scope Telegram-only and dependency-free.
- [x] Document setup, usage, security, and operational limitations.
- [x] Verify frozen lockfile installation in CI.

**Acceptance:** package is discoverable in the workspace and adds no runtime dependencies.

## Phase 1 — Telegram transport and event integration

- [x] Implement Telegram Bot API sendMessage using native fetch().
- [x] Validate token, chat ID, injected fetch, timeout, message length, HTTP response, and Telegram API response.
- [x] Deliver application-formatted plain-text messages through the injected formatter boundary; application-specific event vocabulary and presentation remain with the consumer.
- [x] Exclude raw exchange payloads and high-volume execution reports.
- [x] Serialize sends and expose explicit subscriber cleanup.
- [x] Integrate optional Telegram notifications into Harvester through the composition boundary (PR #734); delivery remains isolated from trading execution.
- [x] Keep notifications disabled when both credentials are absent; reject partial configuration.

**Acceptance:** Telegram is optional, isolated from trading behavior, and usable without adding a runtime dependency.

## Phase 2 — Provider-oriented source layout

- [x] Move all Telegram-specific code and tests under src/telegram/.
- [x] Keep src/index.js limited to stable public re-exports.
- [x] Add src/telegram/index.js as the provider-local export surface.
- [x] Preserve the original formatNotification export as a compatibility alias.
- [x] Keep email/ and discord/ absent until those transports are actually implemented.

**Acceptance:** adding a provider does not scatter provider-specific code across the package root.

## Phase 3 — Reliability hardening and regression coverage

- [x] Ignore callbacks that begin after subscriber shutdown starts.
- [x] Make subscriber close idempotent and attempt every unsubscription even if one fails.
- [x] Attempt cleanup of all successful subscriptions when partial setup fails; preserve the original setup failure.
- [x] Add a configurable maxPending limit to bound the subscriber's local queue.
- [x] Recover the internal send queue after transport or logger failures.
- [x] Avoid duplicate delivery-error logging when a subscriber logger is configured; preserve event-bus reporting when it is not.
- [x] Keep transport validation and bounded delivery inside the package; consuming applications sanitize and bound message content before delivery.
- [x] Redact Telegram credentials from transport and API error messages.
- [x] Reject malformed successful Telegram API responses instead of reporting false success.
- [x] Add deterministic regression tests for shutdown races, partial cleanup, queue overflow, malformed responses, secret redaction, and error recovery.
- [x] Pass package tests and the enforced 90% line / 85% branch coverage gate on the final merged commit.
- [x] Pass workspace tests, syntax, dependency audit, and all required CI checks on the final merged commit.

**Acceptance:** all resource cleanup paths are attempted, local pending work is bounded, failures remain observable, and no test requires real Telegram credentials or network access.

## Phase 4 — Future transports (demand-driven)

- [ ] **Email:** choose a provider/transport only after a consumer defines delivery, authentication, templates, and retry requirements. Keep implementation under src/email/.
- [ ] **Discord:** implement a webhook or bot adapter only after a consumer defines channel routing, payload format, and rate-limit requirements. Keep implementation under src/discord/.
- [ ] Define a shared provider contract only after at least two implemented transports demonstrate common behavior worth standardizing.
- [ ] Add transport-specific tests and coverage gates for every new provider.

**Acceptance:** each provider is independently testable, has clear operational guarantees, and does not introduce unnecessary dependencies into other transports.

## Phase 5 — Delivery guarantees (only when required)

- [ ] Define idempotency and duplicate-send semantics before implementing automatic retries.
- [ ] Add bounded retry/backoff and rate-limit handling if a consumer requires it.
- [ ] Add a persistent outbox only when crash-safe delivery is a product requirement and an appropriate storage owner exists.
- [ ] Add metrics/diagnostics only when their public contract is justified by production usage.

## Decision log

- Telegram is the first adapter because it satisfies the initial operator-alert use case.
- Node.js built-in fetch() is sufficient for Telegram's sendMessage; no SDK is needed.
- No Redis, worker, database, or external queue is included. The subscriber applies a local admission limit and serializes requests.
- No automatic retries: ambiguous network outcomes can produce duplicate messages.
- No subscribeAll(): explicit event allowlists reduce noise and prevent accidental sensitive-data disclosure.
- The package does not read environment variables; consuming applications own configuration and secret loading.
- The package does not promise durable or exactly-once delivery.
- Future provider folders remain absent until implementation begins.

## Completion policy

A roadmap item is complete only after its task PR is merged into develop and required CI checks pass. Never mark a task complete merely because code has been committed or a PR has been opened.

## Harvester Journal Integration Roadmap

---
status: active
type: implementation-roadmap
owner: harvester
---

> **Current-state authority:** this file tracks the staged Journal integration and its remaining Step 8 closeout. Current runtime behavior, event payloads and operational requirements are defined in [Journal Operations](../../apps/harvester/docs/JOURNAL_OPERATIONS.md), [Trading First](../../apps/harvester/docs/TRADING_FIRST.md), and the current [Harvester roadmap](#harvester-journal-integration). Milestone notes below are historical delivery records where a later PR changed the original scope.

> **Current runtime configuration — 2026-11-09:** The application no longer reads `HARVESTER_JOURNAL_ENABLED` or `HARVESTER_JOURNAL_DIRECTORY`. The default application composition always enables Journal and writes to `apps/harvester/logs/`. The PR #473 entry below records the historical environment wiring at that time; it is not current deployment guidance. See [Journal Operations](../../apps/harvester/docs/JOURNAL_OPERATIONS.md#configuration) for the current contract.

## Purpose and priority

This roadmap records the Harvester integration of the existing `@coinzilla/event-bus` and `@coinzilla/journal` packages. The current evidence contract and coverage matrix live in [JOURNAL_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT.md](../../apps/harvester/docs/JOURNAL_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT.md).

**This work does not depend on trading or TESTNET acceptance.** EventBus and Journal record operational lifecycle facts and the selected trading-investigation evidence in issue [#650](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla).

The Journal is an operational observer, not trading-state authority or part of order execution, strategy evaluation, or fill accounting. Its persistence is optional only in configuration-only/no-broker mode. PR #545 added a mandatory account PREFLIGHT gate for every broker-connected startup, including read-only mode: the full account snapshot and account-wide open-order snapshot must be published and durably flushed before market subscriptions or trading-engine activation. After that gate passes, ordinary Journal event delivery remains asynchronous. The separate trading-safety contract requires order-submission and cancellation intent records to be durably flushed before the corresponding broker write; no other Journal I/O is awaited by market, strategy, or fill-accounting workflows. Trading-enabled graceful shutdown also requires a durable CLOSING account snapshot; failure is reported as incomplete shutdown.

Step 1 introduced one EventBus and the best-effort application publisher boundary; it merged into `develop` in [PR #453](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/453). Journal composition and lifecycle publication were added by later milestones: event DTO contracts in [PR #455](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/455), Journal composition in [PR #456](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/456), and process/configuration/broker lifecycle events in [PR #458](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/458). The original Step 1 scope must not be read as the current runtime state; see [Journal Operations](../../apps/harvester/docs/JOURNAL_OPERATIONS.md) for the current event inventory and behavior.

## Audit conclusions

- `@coinzilla/event-bus` already provides in-memory asynchronous fan-out, subscriber isolation, bounded pending deliveries, diagnostics, `flush()`, and `close()`.
- `@coinzilla/journal` already subscribes to EventBus, writes JSONL records through a serialized write queue, reports write failures, and drains/synchronizes on close.
- No shared-package changes are currently justified.
- Harvester already has suitable application boundaries: bootstrap lifecycle, the Conservative trading engine, order submission, sequential user-data processing, canonical Fill accounting, and Portfolio/RecoveryLedger transitions.
- Harvester has an application EventBus boundary, stable lifecycle event names/DTO mappings, an optional asynchronously started Journal service, and process/configuration/broker lifecycle publication.
- Initial lifecycle DTOs contain no financial amounts, so exact decimal-string preservation applies to later order/execution event mappings.
- The former separate application is removed and is not a supported architecture or implementation reference. Preserve only independently documented behavioral requirements, re-specify them within Harvester's own domain boundaries, and never copy a legacy runtime. Harvester's Journal startup and durability rules are defined by this roadmap and `TRADING_FIRST.md`.

See [Architecture — operational event journal](../../apps/harvester/docs/architecture.md#operational-event-journal) and the [AI implementation task](../../apps/harvester/docs/tasks/AI_TASK_JOURNAL_INTEGRATION.md).

## Hard constraints

1. No trading, TESTNET, exchange credentials, orders, or fills are prerequisites for this roadmap. Use offline tests and a read-only/fake broker where useful.
2. Journal initialization is optional only when no broker is connected. Every broker-connected startup requires a ready Journal and durable PREFLIGHT account audit; a query, publication, or durability failure must stop startup before market subscriptions. Ordinary Journal write failures after the PREFLIGHT gate must not synchronously block trading workflows.
3. Never await Journal I/O from market-price evaluation, strategy policy, or fill-accounting processing. The explicit startup PREFLIGHT and trading-enabled CLOSING audits, plus the pre-side-effect order/cancel intent barriers, are the only approved durability waits.
4. Do not put Journal calls in awaited order lifecycle callbacks. Startup PREFLIGHT capture is serialized with early user-data delivery so events cannot race ahead of the account/order baseline; keep this exception confined to startup. The CLOSING audit runs after accepted user-data work has drained.
5. Event publication is best-effort. Catch both synchronous publication exceptions and failed `toResult` outcomes at the application boundary.
6. Keep domain policies pure and broker-independent. Domain code must not import EventBus or Journal.
7. Use object-shaped inputs and object-shaped results for functions. Use `toResult` for fallible workflows where appropriate.
8. Map application facts to small, plain, serializable DTOs. Never publish class instances, SDK objects, secrets, or whole account snapshots.
9. Do not journal every market-price update. Persist meaningful decisions, order transitions, executions, broker acknowledgements, and errors; keep high-frequency market ticks out of the Journal.
10. Keep live trading disabled by default. Default tests remain offline and credential-free.
11. Do not modify shared Journal/EventBus packages unless implementation reveals a reproducible, Harvester-blocking defect. Any such change needs a separate, explicitly justified cross-package task.
12. Every implementation PR must be small, independently testable, and update the relevant documentation and this roadmap in the same PR.

## Proposed event contract

All events use the existing EventBus envelope: generated event ID and timestamp, event name, source, and plain-object data. Use Harvester-owned names and stable business identifiers. Exact field names must be verified against the current source contracts before implementation; examples below are conceptual, not existing APIs.

| Event | Owner / publication point | Minimum useful data | Initial scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `harvester.started` | Process entry point, after runtime startup | broker, mode, enabled markets, trading-enabled flag | Include |
| `harvester.startup_failed` | Process entry point, when startup fails | safe error name/message, startup stage | Include |
| `harvester.stopped` | Process entry point, after shutdown attempt | reason, shutdown outcome | Include |
| `config.validated` | Bootstrap, after validation | non-secret effective settings and enabled markets | Include |
| `broker.connected` / `broker.connection_failed` | Bootstrap around broker connection | broker identifier, outcome, safe error | Include |
| `broker.disconnected` | Bootstrap after disconnect attempt | broker identifier, outcome | Include |
| `broker.status_changed` | Broker/application boundary on meaningful stream transition | stream kind, status, safe reason | Include if source exposes transitions |
| `broker.subscription_established` / `broker.subscription_failed` | Bootstrap around subscriptions | market or stream kind, outcome | Include |
| `market.price_invalid` | Market-data boundary on rejected external data | market, validation reason, safe timestamp | Include |
| `strategy.decision` | Trading engine after meaningful policy result | strategy, market, reference price, reason, allowlisted decision inputs, action summary | Include |
| `strategy.paused` / `strategy.resumed` | Trading engine on actual state transition | market, reason | Include if transition exists |
| `order.submission_requested` | Order use case after local pending registration, before broker call | client order ID, market, side, type, price, quantity | Include |
| `order.submitted` | Order use case after verified canonical acknowledgement | client/exchange order IDs, status | Include |
| `order.updated` | Trading engine after an applied canonical order-state transition | client/exchange order IDs, status, original/executed quantities, cumulative quote quantity where supplied | Include |
| `broker.execution_report` | User-data boundary for each Binance executionReport | versioned allowlisted broker facts, event/transaction times, identifiers, per-event and cumulative quantities, commissions, liquidity flag | Include |
| `order.submission_failed` | Order use case on rejected/unknown outcome | identifiers, classified outcome, safe error | Include |
| `order.cancelled` / `order.cancel_failed` | Cancellation workflow after confirmed outcome | order IDs, final status, reason | Include |
| `execution.fill_applied` | Accounting workflow after successful Fill application | stable fill ID, order ID, market, side, actual price/quantity/fees | Include |
| `execution.rejected` / `execution.accounting_failed` | User-data/accounting boundary | safe identifiers and failure reason | Include |
| `execution.duplicate_ignored` | Fill deduplication boundary | fill ID, order ID | Optional |
| `portfolio.updated` / `position.opened` / `position.closed` | Portfolio transition boundary | market and compact resulting quantities/state | Defer unless a concrete operational question needs them |
| `recovery.cycle_completed` | Conservative recovery completion boundary | market, cycle identifiers, actual realized figures | Include only if a stable transition is exposed |
| `market.price_received` | Market-data boundary | price and market | Do not publish for every update; decision events already carry relevant price |

### Payload rules

- Preserve financial precision. Use canonical decimal strings for prices, quantities, fees, and monetary values.
- Include stable exchange/client order IDs and execution IDs where available.
- Distinguish requested, acknowledged, unknown, rejected, partially filled, and fully filled outcomes.
- An order acknowledgement is not a Fill; only actual normalized Fill facts change Portfolio.
- Do not serialize `Portfolio`, `Position`, `CanonicalOrder`, `Fill`, broker SDK objects, or raw exchange messages directly. Map the minimum required facts into plain DTOs.
- Never include credentials, signed requests, environment variables, or unnecessary account data.
- Avoid duplicate semantic events. If both an order-status transition and a fill are emitted, document their distinct meanings.

## Delivery model: one small PR per step

Do not combine the steps into one large PR. Each PR must contain only its milestone, focused tests, and the documentation/roadmap updates needed to describe the behavior that actually exists.

### Step 1 — Add an application EventBus boundary

**Status:** [x] Implemented, tested in CI, and merged into `develop` by [PR #453](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/453).

**Goal:** Introduce EventBus without changing trading decisions or broker behavior.

**Likely files:** `apps/harvester/package.json`; a focused application event publisher module; bootstrap composition; focused tests; this roadmap.

**Work:**

- Add `@coinzilla/event-bus` as a direct Harvester dependency.
- Construct exactly one EventBus in application composition and inject it explicitly.
- Implement a best-effort publisher that accepts one object argument and returns one object result.
- Catch synchronous publish exceptions and handle failed `toResult` results.
- Log publication failure once through the injected/default shared logger; logger failure must not escape into trading.
- Do not yet add Journal or publish high-volume events.

**Tests:** Accepted event; rejected result; synchronous throw; logger throw; malformed event; publisher never throws into its caller.

**Acceptance:** EventBus is composed once; no global singleton; no domain dependency; no trading behavior change; all publication failure cases are isolated.

**PR boundary:** EventBus dependency + publisher boundary + tests + minimal architecture/roadmap documentation only.

### Step 2 — Define stable Harvester event names and DTO mappings

**Status:** [x] Merged into `develop` by [PR #455](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/455). Current event names and allowlisted payloads are documented in [Journal Operations](../../apps/harvester/docs/JOURNAL_OPERATIONS.md).

**Goal:** Define the application-owned event contract independently of Journal.

**Likely files:** `src/application/events/`; mapping helpers near the relevant application boundary; contract tests; architecture documentation; roadmap.

**Work:**

- Define stable event-name constants and focused DTO mapping functions for the initial process/configuration/broker lifecycle contract.
- Verify current Harvester startup/configuration fields and broker identifier before selecting payload fields; no SDK or domain objects are required for these lifecycle DTOs.
- Use one object input and one object result (`toResult({ data })`).
- Keep deterministic mapping and validation as pure application functions.
- Rely on the existing EventBus publisher boundary for plain-payload validation; EventBus rejects class instances and unsupported built-ins.
- Include safe identifiers; failure DTOs omit stack/cause and redact common labelled secret/token/authorization values.
- No financial amounts occur in these lifecycle DTOs; later financial DTOs must preserve exact decimal strings.
- Do not add event schemas for speculative events.

**Tests:** Every selected event payload; missing identifiers; invalid values; class-instance/unsupported-built-in rejection; secret omission/redaction; JSON serialization. Financial decimal precision is not applicable to this lifecycle-only contract and is required for later financial DTOs.

**Acceptance:** Contract names and payload examples are documented and tested; no EventBus/Journal imports in domain policy modules.

**PR boundary:** Event contract + DTO mapping + tests + documentation. No Journal lifecycle.

### Step 3 — Add optional, non-blocking Journal composition

**Status:** [x] Initial Journal service composition and lifecycle merged into `develop` by [PR #456](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/456). Current broker-connected PREFLIGHT durability requirements and configuration-only/no-broker optionality are defined in [Trading First](../../apps/harvester/docs/TRADING_FIRST.md) and [Journal Operations](../../apps/harvester/docs/JOURNAL_OPERATIONS.md).

**Goal:** Connect the existing Journal to EventBus while keeping trading startup independent.

**Likely files:** `apps/harvester/package.json`; focused Journal preparation/lifecycle helper; `src/index.js` or bootstrap composition; tests; README/operations docs; roadmap.

**Work:**

- Add `@coinzilla/journal` as a direct dependency.
- Construct Journal with the shared EventBus, configured directory, and logger in `prepareOptionalJournal`.
- Start Journal asynchronously during process composition. Configuration-only/no-broker startup may proceed without it; broker-connected startup must complete the PREFLIGHT audit's durable flush before market subscriptions or engine activation.
- Expose `ready`, `status`, and an explicit `close()` operation; report startup/write/close outcomes without allowing logger failures to escape.
- The Journal subscribes only after its directory/session file is ready. Events published before that point are not captured; Steps 1–3 publish no application lifecycle events yet.
- Journal initialization failure must fail any broker-connected startup because the mandatory PREFLIGHT audit cannot be made durable; it must not affect configuration-only/no-broker startup.
- Do not await ordinary Journal record delivery from trading callbacks. Explicit PREFLIGHT/CLOSING account-audit flushes and the separate pre-side-effect order/cancel intent barriers are the only approved durability waits. Coordinated process shutdown draining remains Step 7.

**Tests:** Journal ready/close; invalid directory; pending initialization; construction exception with failing logger; disabled mode; write failure reflected in health status; Harvester startup proceeds while Journal readiness is pending.

**Acceptance:** With Journal unavailable, configuration-only/no-broker startup may proceed. Broker-connected startup must fail before market subscriptions if the PREFLIGHT audit cannot be durably recorded. After successful PREFLIGHT, ordinary trading callbacks do not await Journal writes.

**PR boundary:** Journal construction and optional lifecycle only; no broad event instrumentation.

## Cross-step definition of done

Every implementation PR must:

- Be one small milestone; do not bundle future steps.
- Update this roadmap and relevant docs in the same PR.
- Add deterministic offline tests for success, failure, boundaries, and lifecycle behavior relevant to that step.
- Preserve all existing Harvester tests and trading behavior.
- Demonstrate that Journal is never awaited by the trading workflow.
- Use existing `@coinzilla/utils` helpers and logger; do not duplicate generic helpers.
- Use `toResult` for fallible workflows where appropriate.
- Keep pure calculations, decisions, and deterministic mappings as plain pure functions.
- Use one object argument and one object result for functions.
- Keep strategy policies broker-independent.
- Avoid global `console` usage.
- Keep TESTNET tests opt-in and live trading disabled by default.
- State exact tests/checks run; never claim unrun checks passed.

## Explicit non-goals for this integration

- Durable Portfolio/RecoveryLedger persistence or restart recovery within this observability integration.
- Journal replay as a source of trading state within this observability integration.

A separate Harvester P0 recovery track may consume the Journal as validated recovery evidence; that work must define its own idempotency, ownership, checkpoint, and exchange-reconciliation guarantees. The operational Journal integration remains an observer and does not independently authorize trading.

- Exactly-once delivery.
- Database/outbox infrastructure.
- Every-tick market data capture.
- Notifications, dashboards, or operator control panels.
- Refactoring working strategy/order/accounting code solely to make instrumentation cleaner.
- Changes to shared Journal/EventBus packages without a separately justified defect.

## harvester-roadmap

## Harvester Roadmap

The shutdown-handler regression fixture declares the market-task drain latch in the test that consumes it and removes the unused latch from the separate post-drain safety test; production shutdown behavior is unchanged.

## Harvester Conservative ownership and shutdown incident — issue #1856

- CI follow-up: lifecycle test doubles now return the explicit `{ ok: true, status: "STOPPED" }` runtime-stop contract; ADA replay assertions retain the existing AggregateError contract emitted by the runtime shutdown boundary. No production shutdown behavior was relaxed.

Tracking issue: [#1856](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/1856)
Implementation PR: [#1858](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1858)
Feature branch: `fix/harvester/incident-1856-ownership-shutdown-safety`

### Confirmed source findings

- The durable submission ownership validator was RS-only. It rejected valid CG Conservative recovery SELL ownership even though both strategies share submission-intent and order-registry infrastructure.
- The local order-registration callback logged `SUBMITTED` while the canonical order was still `PENDING`, before the Operational State Store intent and broker placement were confirmed.
- A failed durable submission intent removed its local PENDING registration but did not latch a market pause. Later market events could re-evaluate the same SELL decision and allocate fresh client order IDs.
- Conservative strategy evaluation suppressed a new SELL when any active SELL existed, but did not verify aggregate remaining quantity of active owned SELL orders against net sellable Position inventory after base-asset commissions and `keepQuantity`.
- The strategy shutdown coordinator did not retain timed-out participant wait promises. A later shutdown attempt could start a second `waitUntilSafe()` operation while the first remained unresolved.
- The shutdown handler and outer `createHarvesterStop` boundary awaited asynchronous work without their own bounded deadlines. A pending CLOSING audit or durable `PROCESS_STOPPED` append could leave shutdown waiting indefinitely.

- The shared market-price dispatcher selected any active BUY for Conservative CG trailing-BUY repricing without checking canonical strategy ownership. An RS-owned LINEAUSDT BUY therefore entered the CG path, where the RS-only symbol had no CG pair config and `evaluateTrailingBuyTrigger` dereferenced missing `priceStepPercent`.

- Multi-provider shutdown now returns the same explicit `status: "STOPPED"` acknowledgement as single-provider shutdown, so the outer process boundary can safely publish STOPPED and release account locks.

### Implementation recorded on PR #1858

- Shared market-price dispatch now checks canonical OrderRegistry ownership and invokes the CG-specific trailing-BUY workflow only for CG-owned BUYs. RS-owned and unowned BUY events continue through the shared latest-transition evaluator without dereferencing CG-only pair configuration.
- Shared ownership validation now covers CG Position-scoped ownership and RS Position/cycle-scoped ownership, including strategy, purpose, side and identity checks.
- CG pending-order registration now preserves the originating Position identity and returns the exact registered ownership. Durable Journal `ORDER_SUBMISSION_REQUESTED` facts include that ownership; Operational State Store intent remains a separate durable boundary before broker placement.
- Conflicting supplied ownership metadata is rejected before broker I/O. The registered ownership is used for subsequent durable intent/outcome processing.
- Local order registration is reported as `PENDING`, not `SUBMITTED`. Failed durable intent handling removes the unsubmitted PENDING registration, emits the deferral, and latches the affected symbol with `ORDER_INTENT_NOT_DURABLE`; a regression proves a later tick does not allocate another client order ID or call the broker.
- Conservative active SELL aggregation includes PENDING/UNKNOWN reservations and is checked against net sellable inventory after commissions and `keepQuantity`.
- Strategy shutdown participant waits are single-flight. Timeout/abort retains the underlying operation in a shared pending map; retries cannot overlap it and safety cannot be reported while it remains pending.
- Shutdown phases have bounded deadlines and abort signals. Pending phases are exposed in diagnostics and block overlapping retries.
- Durable `PROCESS_STOPPED` has its own 30-second deadline and pending-append guard. Runtime completion, durable STOPPED, OS process exit and process-lock release remain distinct.
- `JOURNAL_OPERATIONS.md` documents the separate Operational State Store, Journal, legacy order-history and relational trading-history responsibilities, startup audit/readiness distinction, shutdown phase deadlines and fail-closed durability behavior.

- Strategy evaluation already reads active COIN_GRABBER SELLs from the registry. The new final

  before the broker call; it proves intent creation, not that the broker request was sent.
- ACKNOWLEDGED submissions update the registry; uncertain outcomes become UNKNOWN and pause the
  market. A definite rejection removes the pending reservation. A definite post-only rejection
  also invalidates the market book. After a definite filter rejection, the next evaluation

  pause the market. These failure paths are independently covered; temporal proximity does not

## Conservative trading correctness and exhaustive scenario coverage — issue #1763

**Objective:** prove Conservative trading calculations, accounting, lifecycle transitions and safety decisions with source-mapped deterministic evidence. This complements (does not replace) focused unit tests and existing application/replay tests. The canonical [Conservative Domain Specification](../../apps/harvester/docs/domain/CONSERVATIVE_DOMAIN_SPECIFICATION.md) remains the sole behavior authority; the [scenario-test guide](../../apps/harvester/docs/domain/CONSERVATIVE_DOMAIN_SCENARIO_TESTS.md) defines authoring conventions; [issue #1763](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/1763) owns the exhaustive matrix and phase-by-phase evidence.

**Non-negotiable quality bar**

- Exact decimal inputs and independently derived expected values; no floating-point arithmetic in financial test oracles.
- Real domain objects/components for the behavior under test; mock only external ports at application boundaries.
- Every meaningful state transition proves complete state, accounting deltas, emitted intents/dispositions, idempotency, conflict rejection and failure atomicity.
- Every financial invariant is checked across Portfolio, Position, RecoveryLedger, fills and order execution/commitment projections.
- Offline, deterministic, credential-free by default. No live/TESTNET order operations or exchange writes.
- No invented or changed trading rule. Unresolved or unsupported behavior is recorded as blocked/unsupported until an explicit contract decision exists.

**Execution strategy:** one small, reviewable PR per vertical slice. Prefer a test-only RED PR followed by the smallest GREEN production+test PR when a real defect is found. Do not combine unrelated domains or broad refactors. Each PR updates the issue matrix and evidence; the roadmap is synchronized at phase boundaries.

### Small-PR operating protocol

For each slice:

1. Select one or a few related matrix rows and identify the authoritative spec clauses and source owner.
2. Inspect existing tests and reuse existing canonical factories. Record why current tests do or do not prove the requirement.
3. Write a failing regression test first when a defect is suspected; assert the business invariant, not an implementation call.
4. Run the narrowest deterministic test target, then relevant package tests and required workspace checks.
5. If production code must change, keep the change minimal and preserve public behavior outside the specified defect.
6. Run the exact relevant suite again; record RED/GREEN evidence, test path, commit/PR and exact verified head SHA.
7. Update #1763 matrix status and the domain test inventory. Do not mark a row covered until evidence is merged to develop and required CI passes.
8. Keep each PR independently reviewable and revertible. Avoid drive-by cleanup, unrelated renames and broad fixture rewrites.

### Coverage status vocabulary

- **COVERED:** named test path and assertions verified on merged develop with required CI evidence.
- **PARTIAL:** some dimensions are tested, but boundary, accounting, state, failure or interaction proof is incomplete.
- **MISSING:** applicable requirement has no adequate executable evidence.
- **BLOCKED:** cannot be tested safely until a specification/product/architecture decision or prerequisite exists; include owner and unblock condition.
- **UNSUPPORTED:** explicitly outside the supported contract; cite the reason and do not fabricate behavior.

### Release/initiative completion gate

Do not claim 100% correctness from line/branch coverage. Completion means every applicable canonical rule and risk row is mapped to adequate executable evidence at the correct layer; every financial invariant and lifecycle transition is protected; all known gaps are closed or explicitly blocked/unsupported; no test oracle derives expected results from the implementation under test; and required CI passes on the exact merged head. Coverage percentages remain useful diagnostics, not the acceptance definition.

## Conservative Operational State submission barrier (#1743)

- Complete in merged [PR #1750](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1750) (exact head `6150d93e51c4803f89f7b1abef09ac40f1edd6a7`; merge commit `f0c2d42e1a78137c1233e45b3a4f513da6ddbb0a`). The archived 49-record session contains zero `ORDER_SUBMISSION_INTENT` and zero `ORDER_SUBMISSION_OUTCOME` facts. Source confirmed the Conservative engine supplied application callback names where the executor expected durable callback names, allowing the optional callbacks to be absent. The fix maps the canonical callback pair and makes the barrier mandatory when the Operational State Store is configured. It preserves the archived fill, projector ownership checks, and disabled restart restoration. All 30 applicable exact-head checks passed; the read-only TESTNET check was skipped. No exchange operations were performed. The diagnostic runbook and incident wording are being refreshed in the documentation consolidation PR.
- Root cause: Conservative passed `onOperationalStateSubmissionIntent` / `onOperationalStateSubmissionOutcome` to an executor that accepts `onDurableSubmissionIntent` / `onDurableSubmissionOutcome`. The optional executor callbacks were therefore absent on the order path even while the Operational State Store was configured.
- Fix: map the canonical callback names, require the pair at engine activation whenever the store exists, and enforce the requirement again inside the executor. Regression coverage proves intent-before-broker ordering, fail-closed intent persistence, and rejection of missing callbacks. Existing tests continue to own definite rejection, UNKNOWN outcome, outcome-write failure, and local-acknowledgement ordering.

This is observational history only: it does not adopt orders, infer strategy ownership, restore process state, authorize trading, or certify delisted/unconfigured-market or exchange-retention completeness.

**Filled-order history — MERGED:** [PR #1469](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1469) merged into `develop` as `39f098000d6c20cb596a9e6700250faa00bbd80e` (exact validated PR head `6d11d883e2d8250c2b3fab9f6d5a40d6178996bb`). It delivers a non-authoritative `harvester_orders` projection. Persist an order as soon as cumulative executed quantity is positive, including immediate partial/fully filled acknowledgements, later partial/final fills, and partial-fill cancellation outcomes. Further lifecycle snapshots update the same row. At merge time the projection identity was `(environment, providerInstanceId, providerType, accountId, clientOrderId)`; that client-ID-only identity is superseded by the market-scoped exchange-order identity correction in PR #1849. Exact decimal strings, canonical market/asset facts, provider/account provenance, and available strategy/position ownership remain retained.

Order and fill observers use bounded serialized best-effort queues. SQLite is never awaited from broker submission, user-data processing, fill application, accounting, Journal, or trading readiness. Queue overflow and write errors are reported as history gaps without blocking trading. TESTNET/LIVE retain separate database files. OrderRegistry, Journal, and ADR-0001 retain their existing authority and guarantees; no restart restoration is introduced.

The temporary `harvester_processes` process-ID smoke-test row and its obsolete persistence helper are removed. Neither process ID nor runtime session ID is part of the order-history record or key. No changes are made to `packages/db`.

### Ownership and dependency direction

- Harvester owns trading-history schemas, repository semantics, migrations, lifecycle projections, and SQLite composition.
- `packages/db` owns only generic provider-neutral persistence contracts and adapters.
- OrderRegistry remains authoritative for in-process order ownership/state.
- Journal remains the ordered lifecycle evidence store; this is not a second event ledger.
- ADR-0001 remains separate and unchanged. The projection does not restore/adopt orders after restart.
- SQLite is the only currently implemented provider.

**Routine relational-history backups, restore verification, bounded retention and backup-file permissions — COMPLETE:** [#1564](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/1564) was delivered in merged [PR #1567](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1567), merge commit `5f1d4a035941db8a7e0d6cd3c401299ab3c6ef21`. Host scheduling remains operator-owned. Main-database permission enforcement, disk/WAL monitoring, disk-full and corruption response, and encrypted off-host replication remain deferred.

### Remaining persistence work after Phase 3

1. Filtered account snapshot history only with explicit provenance and completeness semantics.
2. Offline, idempotent historical imports from verified source evidence.
3. **Versioned trading-history query API and Dashboard consumer — COMPLETE (#1635, #1634; merged PR #1636).** Existing orders, individual fills and commission facts are exposed through Harvester-owned application queries and an authenticated in-process `/api/v1` HTTP listener. The Angular Dashboard consumes the same versioned contract for read-only Orders, Fills and Commissions pages. Harvester owns the shared database connection and listener lifecycle; no separate API process, schema changes, sessions/errors tables, trading controls or exchange operations. All required checks passed on exact head `38e26aca14e8c146ea974dbf42fe133524ad83c6`; the advisory External Documentation Links workflow also passed; issues #1634 and #1635 are closed.

**Explicit exclusions from #1554/#1556:** no account-wide or delisted-market history completeness claim, account snapshots as a history source, strategy-cycle lifecycle, PnL/analytics, equity/drawdown snapshots, process-restart restoration/adoption, Journal replay, new providers, `sessions`/`errors` tables, broker order-mutation behavior changes, Journal semantics changes, ADR-0001 rewrite, or exchange operations.

### P0 — Conservative ADA recovery lifecycle (#1359)

The 2026-11-17 Binance TESTNET cycle is preserved in merged [session audit PR #1358](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1358). The exact evidence shows two 50 ADA BUY fills, 0.05 ADA base-asset commission on each BUY, a 99.8 ADA recovery SELL, net realized profit of 0.04910062 USDT against the configured 0.05 USDT minimum, and 0.1 ADA left over. The remainder is valid against the 0.1 ADA quantity step/minimum but is below the 5 USDT minimum notional; it must be classified as MIN_NOTIONAL dust, not quantity-increment dust. The 0.1% TESTNET versus 0.075% LIVE commission configuration is an operator configuration mismatch, not a defect in the fee-rate formula.

## Proposed strategy — Recovery Seller (RS)

**Status: RS-1 through RS-5 offline acceptance COMPLETE in PR #1515.** RS-4 production runtime dispatch, engine-owned order submission, account-wide quote/base authorization, RS BUY ownership and terminal mixed-SELL reconciliation are composed through the shared serialized Trading Engine. The scoped RS-5 offline matrix covers BUY-to-SELL lifecycle composition, sole-cycle reservation, duplicate suppression, terminal reconciliation, atomic recovery/legacy accounting, next-cycle gating, same-/different-market CG/RS accounting concurrency, Spot/EARN custody, fixed legacy basis, exchange filters, unknown outcomes and fail-closed failures. `RECOVERY_SELLER_RUNTIME_ACCEPTANCE_COMPLETE` is now `true`; the operator pair map declares the approved LINEAUSDT TESTNET configuration and the RS strategy configuration is globally `enabled: true`; the per-market selector still excludes LINEAUSDT from LIVE. Restart/replay and third-asset commission valuation are deferred. STOP is terminal; CC-operator exposes authorized read-only status only and cannot clear, reset, unpause or resume it. No TESTNET/LIVE exchange operations were performed.

- **Goal:** progressively reduce explicitly authorized legacy Spot inventory through recovery cycles. Each cycle acquires recovery inventory and may sell it with the eligible configured legacy slice only when the independent recovery, applicable legacy and combined-cycle profitability gates all pass.
- **Accepted input direction:** per-pair `sellQuantity` plus `legacyPosition.invested` and `legacyPosition.quantity`; RS calculates average historical cost itself. Example: 100 USDT / 50 ZRO = 2 USDT/ZRO. The full logical legacy quantity need not remain in Spot; EARN-held inventory is unavailable for Spot SELL until returned and authoritatively reconciled.
- **Concurrent operation:** RS and CG may run at the same time, including on the same market when both are enabled. They use a shared Portfolio that supports multiple independent Positions per market, with stable strategy/Position ownership and centralized quote/base custody and reservations through the shared Trading Engine. Positions are independent accounting units, not separate wallets; aggregate spendable inventory remains bounded by authoritative exchange balances. No blanket strategy mutual-exclusion lock or mandatory handoff is allowed.
- **Delivery order:** RS-1 Conservative source audit is complete (audit only; no code moved); RS-2a shared Portfolio/multi-Position foundation is complete in PR #1118; RS-2b accounting, verified custody, canonical mixed SELL allocation, terminal reconciliation, atomic dual projections, shared snapshot baselines and application-level reservation release/profitability integration are complete in PRs #1131, #1137, #1144, #1152, #1153, #1203, #1212, #1213, #1262 and #1276. RS-3 pure policy is complete in PR #1127: PR #1325 merged sticky STOP/lifecycle foundations; PR #1379 merged independent profitability gates and mixed-SELL planning; PR #1127 implements pair-configured `minProfit`, Conservative-compatible `LIMIT_MAKER`/`LIMIT` selection and fee reserves, and global STOP for supported exchange-filter violations. Exact implementation head `96315757e74a4851770716b04d8dae5cf9580ece` passed 13/13 RS evaluator tests, 2,101/2,101 Harvester tests, workspace tests/coverage, strict ESLint, syntax, actionlint and dependency audit. Post-fill adverse results and terminal partial/canceled outcomes remain fail-closed with terminal STOP; third-asset valuation is deferred and CC-operator has no reset/resume capability; see the [CG-to-RS policy blocker audit](../../apps/harvester/docs/domain/RECOVERY_SELLER_POLICY_BLOCKERS.md). RS-4 production dispatch and account-wide commitment authorization are implemented in PR #1515. Same-/different-market accounting concurrency, BUY-fill → runtime SELL → sole reservation/registration → duplicate-transition suppression, terminal mixed-SELL reconciliation, reservation release and next-cycle gating are covered by offline tests. The acceptance gate is open; RS is enabled by default and each market remains restricted by its own `tradingEnvironment`. Exact-head required CI is the final merge check. Shared-function extraction is not a standalone phase: extract only when RS has a concrete need, with characterization tests and CG regression coverage in the same change.
- **Settled first-implementation contract:** `sellQuantity` is additive legacy quantity; original legacy average cost is calculated once and stays fixed while remaining legacy quantity decreases by the actual amount sold; smaller remainders may be sold when all gates pass; exchange-filter dust is retained and excluded from later RS calculations; recovery-only cycles continue after legacy exhaustion; operator configuration supplies historical basis/authorization before startup; Conservative BUY cadence, tranche sizing, investment-limit behavior and third-asset fee valuation are reused; budgets are independent per strategy and pair while actual balances/reservations remain shared; an investment limit blocks new BUYs but leaves existing recovery SELLs alive; advanced lifecycle controls are deferred under FITDIB. See the canonical [RS specification](../../apps/harvester/docs/domain/recovery-seller-domain-specification.md) and [implementation roadmap](../../apps/harvester/docs/domain/recovery-seller-implementation-roadmap.md).
- **Merged PR #1137 — first verified-Spot plumbing slice:** `AccountSnapshot` carries a separate additional tracked-base baseline, the snapshot manager accepts the independently sourced allocation, and the shared order allocator reconciles its delta and combined SELL reservations without inserting legacy quantity into Portfolio. This does not create the verified legacy custody source or mixed Fill allocation.
- **Merged PR #1144 — immutable order ownership metadata:** extends `OrderRegistry` with immutable strategy/Position/purpose/cycle attribution, keyed by Harvester `clientOrderId` and linked to `brokerOrderId` after acknowledgement. It rejects conflicting owners and preserves attribution through broker updates and ambiguous lifecycle states. This is an in-memory registry contract only; it does not yet wire RS order submission, fill allocation, durable restart restoration, or executable RS behavior.
- **Merged PR #1152 — verified legacy Spot allocation:** adds the pure calculation that subtracts every Portfolio Position's base quantity from the authoritative Spot total and caps the remainder at original/remaining legacy authorization. The snapshot manager supplies immutable canonical balances and Portfolio to the injectable source. This is not wired to RS runtime configuration and does not enable execution.
- **Merged PR #1153 — canonical mixed SELL allocation metadata:** creates immutable application metadata bound to the original canonical Fill ID/fingerprint and registered order ownership. It splits recovery/legacy gross quantities, actual quote proceeds and commissions exactly without creating synthetic Fills or mutating Portfolio/legacy state.

Exact head `19448d63d117f563c31d8ab9422ac73623974782` passed 1,847/1,847 Harvester tests and all required checks. Confirmed fills are still committed when any applicable profitability gate is false; no complete RS policy, runtime registration or order submission is added.
- **Safety:** PRs #1118–#1379 establish the shared Portfolio, accounting, independent profitability, SELL price-planning, STOP/lifecycle and BUY-policy foundations; merged PR #1127 completes the pure pre-submission SELL evaluator and its owner-approved order-type, fee-reserve and exchange-filter STOP policy. Earlier accounting/policy foundations did not register or enable RS. The production runtime dispatch path, shared account-wide quote/base authorization and terminal mixed-SELL reconciliation are implemented in PR #1515. Scoped RS-5 offline lifecycle/concurrency/failure proof is complete and the runtime acceptance gate is open; RS is enabled by default and each market remains restricted by its own `tradingEnvironment`. Restart/replay and third-asset valuation are deferred. STOP is terminal with read-only CC-operator visibility and no clear/resume capability. Exact-head CI is the final merge check. ## Harvester source, domain correctness and documentation audit — issue #1093

**Status: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — merged in [PR #1094](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1094) on 2026-11-13; issue #1093 is closed.** The audit starts from current `develop` baseline `9989fea9f77f9ce4b506d4658f2ff1ddef516d83` (309 Harvester JavaScript files: 162 production and 147 test files). The PR head inventory is 312 files (164 production and 148 test files), including two independently tested pure domain guards. The domain-only inventory is 35 production files and 30 test files. Scope is `apps/harvester/**` and Harvester/project documentation only; no shared package, other application, trading economics, or runtime trading configuration changed.

### Confirmed defects corrected test-first

1. **Third-asset commission baseline ordering was reversed.** The workflow previously persisted `EXECUTION_FILL_APPLIED` before the targeted `COMMISSION_BASELINE`. It now records each required fee-asset baseline first, then the fill fact, then commits the in-memory Portfolio/RecoveryLedger projection. A baseline persistence failure does not discard a valid fill; the later account audit still fails closed when required evidence is absent.
2. **Targeted commission-baseline facts accepted invalid snapshots.** The durable-facts schema now requires a complete audit and exactly one fee-asset balance; empty, multi-asset, and incomplete targeted baselines are rejected.
3. **Normal user-data SELL fills did not forward terminal order evidence.** The normal `order-event-workflow` completion path now forwards the exact reconciled canonical SELL. The cancellation/reconciliation race and exchange-constrained dust paths also pass their canonical terminal SELL.
4. **Recovery completion could be evaluated without a canonical terminal SELL.** A shared pure guard requires `CanonicalOrder`, SELL side, FILLED status, broker identity, exact executed/original quantity equality, and matching market. Both durable completion recorders use the same guard.
5. **Dust evidence was insufficiently validated.** Exchange filter thresholds must be positive and evaluated values must satisfy the reason-specific contract. `MIN_NOTIONAL` requires a positive evaluated notional when evaluated quantity is positive; `QUANTITY_INCREMENT` accepts a zero rounded quantity only when the actual residual is smaller than one full step. Valid zero evaluation for a `MIN_QUANTITY`-limited residual remains supported; contradictory evidence fails closed.
6. **Fill accounting and cycle completion could race.** Both transitions now share one queue. Completion waits for earlier durable fill updates, stages both immutable projections, persists the cycle outcome, and only then commits the paired in-memory reset.
7. **Canonical timestamp validation was inconsistent.** A pure `isCanonicalNonNegativeSafeInteger` helper now rejects negative zero, negative, fractional, unsafe, and non-number timestamps. MarketPrice, MarketBook, AccountSnapshot, VolatilityCandle, account snapshot reconciliation, account fact recording, and market-history coverage use the same contract.
8. **Symbol configuration generation was unnecessarily restrictive.** Binance metadata retrieval now preserves available order types and pair configuration validates only the mode selected by the configured maker policy: zero maker assumption requires `LIMIT_MAKER`; non-zero uses `LIMIT`.
9. **Invalid `TRADING_MODE` silently selected TESTNET.** The symbol generator still defaults to TESTNET when unset, but rejects any explicitly configured value other than `testnet` or `live`.
10. **Small exchange-aligned quantities could fail numeric conversion.** The generator now expands JavaScript exponent notation before exact decimal comparison, preserving small values without accepting precision loss.
11. **Market-history and account-baseline use-case coverage was thin.** Regression tests now cover invalid ports/inputs, malformed record collections, regressing verification time, reconciliation failure/mismatch, incomplete audit evidence, non-durable append, failed/mismatched readback, and invalid baseline inputs.

### Test-first and verification evidence

- Test-only RED runs reproduced the targeted commission-baseline schema defects, missing terminal SELL evidence, contradictory dust evidence, negative-zero MarketPrice/MarketBook timestamps, and the start-harvester terminal-order forwarding regression.
- The Harvester suite passed **1,512/1,512** on verification commit `af0f32f8494c0aa51b95472bdbc0d1ed832185e9`. The coverage workflow passed at **81.45% line, 81.23% branch, and 80.63% function coverage**. This report aggregates Harvester with imported workspace packages (brokers, entities, event-bus, journal, notifiers, and utils); it is not an isolated Harvester-only metric. The aggregate remains below the 90% branch target noted in project guidance; Harvester has no package-specific threshold. Isolating and enforcing a 90% Harvester-only branch gate is a separate scoped task; no threshold was weakened or changed.
- At this historical audit checkpoint, changed-file ESLint/syntax checks passed and no lint rules were weakened. The former style-only workspace baseline has since been eliminated; strict full-workspace `pnpm lint` now passes with zero errors and warnings (PR #1288), with rule hardening in PR #1311. No outstanding ESLint cleanup remains.
- All six required `develop` checks and the advisory external documentation-link check passed on exact verification head `af0f32f8494c0aa51b95472bdbc0d1ed832185e9`: Run package tests, Workspace test coverage, Check JavaScript syntax, packages/utils tests, Audit production dependencies, actionlint, and Check external documentation links. The optional read-only Binance TESTNET integration was skipped.
- The PR updates the Conservative Domain Specification, architecture/recovery flow, broker port/adapter contract, accounting invariant matrix, domain test inventory, symbol-generator instructions, and a dated audit report. Documentation describes the implemented source behavior rather than planned behavior.
- Large-file modularity review and staged extraction plans are recorded in Section 7 of the audit report; no broad state-machine or durable-store rewrite was bundled into this correctness PR.

### Scope and remaining work

The current coverage workflow includes shared workspace dependencies, so it cannot report a clean Harvester-only branch percentage. Add an app-local coverage report and enforce the 90% branch target for Harvester in a separate focused task. Start with uncovered branches in the account snapshot manager, conservative engine/workflow, broker metadata adapter, and operational recovery scripts; keep each change behavior-preserving and test-first. This PR intentionally does not modify shared packages to raise the workspace aggregate.

High-risk accounting, durable-facts, recovery, market-data, configuration, and operational-script boundaries received the detailed source review. The remaining style-only lint baseline is deliberately separated from these correctness fixes; do not mass-autofix unrelated modules or weaken strict rules.

## High-volatility protection — issue #1016

**Status: PROTECTION IMPLEMENTED; regression matrix, exact-head CI, candle-stream freshness correction (PR #1049), and local offline calibration CLI (PR #1046) are merged; representative historical threshold calibration remains open.** This is the immediate Harvester safety priority. The canonical behavior and delivery contract are in [Volatility Protection](../../apps/harvester/docs/volatility-protection.md).

- Per-market protection; one volatile pair must not stop another.
- Use completed 1-minute UTC candles, ATR(14) with Wilder smoothing, NATR, and a current/reference ratio against the previous 60 completed NATR observations.
- Load approximately 100 completed candles per enabled market at startup; maintain the series from live Kline updates and backfill gaps after reconnect.
- Missing, stale, invalid, insufficient or discontinuous candle data blocks new strategy activity. It is never treated as low volatility.
- While protected, block all new BUY and non-recovery strategy actions. Cancel only Harvester-owned, acknowledged active BUYs through the existing durable cancellation and fill-reconciliation path.
- Preserve resting recovery SELLs without volatility-driven cancellation or repricing. Continue SELL fills/accounting and permit only recovery SELL lifecycle actions needed to recover invested capital.
- Enforce protection centrally immediately before broker submission; identify recovery SELL intent explicitly rather than allowing every SELL.
- Initial ratio thresholds (warning 1.5, protect 2.0, recover 1.3 for 3 completed candles) are provisional pending offline historical validation.
- Do not alter Conservative recovery economics or imply process-restart recovery is complete. No exchange operations are authorized.

## Adaptive price step — volatility-adjusted spacing

**Status: PROPOSED — STRATEGY POLICY NOT FROZEN; NOT IMPLEMENTED.** This is a strategy enhancement proposal, not permission to change current trading behavior. The configured `priceStepPercent` remains the strategy baseline. Harvester may derive an effective step from a normalized volatility coefficient supplied by the shared [Indicators package](../../packages/indicators/README.md). The package now provides parameterized ATR, NATR and volatility-ratio calculations; adaptive-step reference-window, coefficient bounds, baseline-floor and order-replacement policy remain open.

### Intended behavior

- At reference volatility, the coefficient is neutral (`1.0`) and the effective step equals the configured baseline.
- When current volatility is 1.5 times its reference level, the illustrative coefficient is `1.5`; a baseline of `0.5%` therefore produces an effective step of `0.75%`.
- The configured baseline is never overwritten. The strategy consumes a derived effective value for the decisions explicitly included in the final scope.
- Whether lower volatility may reduce the baseline, or whether the baseline is a hard floor, remains an open policy decision.
- Calculate volatility independently for each market. Do not compare raw ATR values across symbols with different price scales.
- The indicator calculation must not know about Binance DTOs, order placement, Harvester positions, fees or strategy policy.

### Proposed calculation model (illustrative, not yet accepted)

Normalize ATR to the instrument's price level:

`ATR% = ATR / Close × 100`

Compare a current normalized ATR value with a reference value for the same market and timeframe:

`VolatilityCoefficient = CurrentATR% / ReferenceATR%`

Then derive:

`EffectivePriceStepPercent = ConfiguredPriceStepPercent × VolatilityCoefficient`

Example: configured step `0.5%`, reference ATR `1.0%`, current ATR `1.5%`; coefficient `1.5`, effective step `0.75%`. This is an example of the intended relationship, not a frozen formula or parameter set. Raw ATR is an absolute price movement and must not be multiplied directly into a percentage-based `priceStepPercent`.

### Ownership boundary

- The `@coinzilla/indicators` package owns exchange-neutral, deterministic indicator calculations over normalized candle data (ATR, NATR and volatility ratio).
- Harvester owns the policy: candle timeframe and history requirements, reference window, coefficient bounds/smoothing, fallback behavior, configuration, which strategy decisions use the value, and when orders may be recalculated.
- Brokers owns exchange-specific market-data retrieval and DTO adaptation. Indicator code must not import broker or exchange SDKs.
- Existing orders must not be silently repriced when a new indicator value arrives. Any order replacement policy must be separately specified and tested.
- Exchange tick/step filters remain authoritative after strategy spacing is calculated.

### Design questions to resolve before implementation

1. **Consumer reference:** rolling reference window and how the baseline adapts across market regimes.
2. **Timeframe and cadence:** candle interval, refresh frequency and whether the coefficient is stable between closed candles.
3. **Reference:** rolling reference window and how the baseline adapts across market regimes.
4. **Timeframe and cadence:** candle interval, refresh frequency and whether the coefficient is stable between closed candles.
5. **Coefficient policy:** exact ratio, neutral point, smoothing/hysteresis and treatment of sudden volatility spikes.
6. **Bounds:** minimum/maximum coefficient and effective step; decide whether low volatility can reduce the configured baseline.
7. **Fallback:** behavior for missing, stale, insufficient, invalid or discontinuous market data. Never silently treat unavailable volatility as zero.
8. **Strategy scope:** Conservative/Aggressive applicability and the exact BUY/SELL decisions affected.
9. **Observability/configuration:** diagnostics for baseline, indicator inputs, reference, coefficient, effective step and fallback reason; opt-in/disabled-by-default rollout.
10. **Validation:** historical/offline evidence, multi-symbol behavior, restart/recovery interaction, precision/tick-size and a separately approved TESTNET plan.

### Proposed delivery sequence

1. [x] Define the package boundary, completed-candle contract and exact-decimal calculation behavior in the Indicators package.
2. [x] Create the Indicators workspace package and public API for ATR, NATR and volatility ratio — [PR #1018](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1018).
3. [ ] Submit a separate Harvester consumer change for configuration, strategy policy and effective-step integration.
5. [ ] Add regression coverage for multiple markets, invalid/stale history, bounds, smoothing, order lifecycle and unchanged behavior when disabled.
6. [ ] Validate against historical/offline market data; consider TESTNET only under a separately approved bounded plan.

**Safety constraints:** this roadmap item changes no runtime behavior. No coefficient, timeframe, period, bound or fallback is finalized. The feature remains unimplemented and disabled until the design, tests and acceptance criteria are agreed. No TESTNET/LIVE operation is authorized by this planning work.

## Operator tooling — interactive trading-pair configuration generator

**Status: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — delivered in [PR #1012](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/pull/1012).**

**Problem:** manually adding a pair requires looking up exchange-specific precision and trading filters. Guessing tick size, quantity step, minimum quantity or minimum notional can produce invalid configuration and rejected orders.

**Command:** `pnpm run config:symbol` (also available from the repository root through `pnpm --filter @coinzilla/harvester config:symbol`).

**Canonical destination:** merge the generated pair into `apps/harvester/config/strategies/cg-coin-grabber.js` at `CG_COIN_GRABBER_CONFIG.pairs.<SYMBOL>`. `config/index.js` composes this named strategy export into the single application-wide `appConfig`; do not create parallel runtime configuration boundaries.

**Operator inputs:** symbol, quote investment budget, `keepQuantity`, maker percentage, taker percentage, minimum profit (quote units), and price-step percentage; both are required strategy inputs because their values are market-specific and must not be guessed. Derive `orderQuantity` from the quote budget and a current public ticker-price snapshot, rounded down to the exchange step and capped by active maximum quantity/notional bounds. Derive price/quantity precision from Binance filters and check the reference price against active minimum/maximum price bounds.

**Safety and validation:**

- Use public, read-only Binance Spot `exchangeInfo` and `ticker/price`; select TESTNET (`https://testnet.binance.vision`) or LIVE (`https://api.binance.com`) explicitly. Default to TESTNET unless the shell's `TRADING_MODE` is `live`; no API credentials or order endpoints. Generate against the same environment Harvester will use because symbols/filters can differ. Reject active symbol/exchange filters outside the currently validated LIMIT/LIMIT_MAKER subset; ignore only filters exclusive to unsupported order types. Account-specific `myFilters` remain a runtime startup check because this generator intentionally requires no credentials. The preview records the public metadata source and fetch timestamp.
- Require an existing, actively trading Spot symbol and the LIMIT/LIMIT_MAKER order types used by Harvester.
- Preserve exact decimal strings while parsing inputs and calculating order quantity. Reject malformed/negative/non-finite values, invalid percentages, a budget below minimum notional, quantities below minimum quantity, and `keepQuantity` not aligned to `LOT_SIZE.stepSize`.
- Keep maker/taker assumptions as separate operator inputs; do not treat public exchange metadata as account commission data.
- Generate a complete pair object and validate the merged application configuration with the runtime `validateAppConfig` contract.
- New pairs are enabled by default. Refuse an already configured symbol; never silently replace an existing pair.
- Serialize writes under an exclusive lock and atomically replace `config/strategies/cg-coin-grabber.js`; preserve all existing pairs and unrelated strategy settings. On errors, leave the original config intact and clean up temporary files/locks owned by this invocation.
- Show the generated pair and exchange constraints for operator review before writing. Declining confirmation changes nothing.

**Implementation and verification checklist:**

1. [x] Inspect/reuse the canonical config loader/schema and public decimal utilities; keep the CLI and Binance adapter at the application tooling boundary.
2. [x] RED/GREEN — symbol/input validation, percentage boundaries, exact decimal sizing, exchange precision and min/max/notional boundaries.
3. [x] RED/GREEN — mocked Binance exchange-info/ticker responses, unsupported symbols/status/order types, malformed/duplicate filters, HTTP/JSON/network failures.
4. [x] RED/GREEN — complete config generation, runtime-schema validation, enabled-by-default behavior and existing-pair preservation.
5. [x] RED/GREEN — interactive confirmation/cancellation, atomic persistence, lock contention, malformed existing config and cleanup on failure.
6. [x] Register the package command; document prompts, defaults, generated fields, safety behavior and operator invocation.
7. [x] Run Harvester tests/coverage and all required repository CI on the exact PR head. No TESTNET/LIVE order activity is needed or authorized for this feature.

**Verification:** exact PR head `a680ad6e612d088c3565beae9b039618f1496a20` passed the full Harvester suite (1,025/1,025), workspace package tests, Harvester/workspace coverage, JavaScript syntax, actionlint, production dependency audit, Utils tests and external documentation links. The optional read-only Binance TESTNET integration workflow was skipped; no live/testnet trading or order placement was performed.

**Acceptance:** the operator supplies strategy-owned inputs without guessing exchange filters; the generator obtains and validates Binance Spot metadata, creates a complete runtime-valid enabled pair in the canonical config, and cannot silently overwrite existing pair settings or leave a partial config after failure.

## Conservative strategy correctness — prioritized fix plan (2026-11-11)

> **Status: PLANNED — findings require implementation and exact-head verification.** Scope: `apps/harvester`, Conservative strategy only. Financial correctness takes priority over trading availability. One behavior/invariant per PR; RED regression first, minimal GREEN correction second; focused tests and required CI on the exact final PR head. No Binance connection or TESTNET/LIVE operation is part of these steps. Do not enable unattended restart/resumption before its separate recovery gate is complete.

### Implementation order

1. **P0 — Prevent competing same-symbol orders when an external order is open** — [#985](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/985).
2. **P0 — Preserve exact fill accounting and commission valuation**, especially third-asset commissions and live/DTO/replay parity — [#654](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/654), finding F-039.
3. **P0 — Prove recovery SELL lifecycle and cycle completion** under partial fills, cancel/fill races, UNKNOWN outcomes and missing durable completion facts — [#654](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/654), finding F-041.
4. **P1 — Close residual quantity/notional/dust boundaries** and prevent unchanged invalid-order retry loops.
5. **P0 before unattended restart — Complete durable restore and exchange reconciliation** — [#654](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/654), umbrella [#626](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/626). This is a separate release gate; it does not authorize early resumption.

---

### P0.1 — Block new strategy orders when an unowned external order is open on the same symbol

**Problem:** the owned OrderRegistry is not the account-wide open-order set. A manually placed or otherwise unowned order can already be working while the strategy sees no owned order and submits a competing order. External orders must remain unowned and untouched, but must be considered by the strategy's safety gate. This is a symbol-level conflict, not a reason to disable unrelated markets.

**Tracking:** [issue #985](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/985).

**Relevant code:** [conservative-trading-engine.js](../../apps/harvester/src/use-cases/conservative-trading-engine.js) (decision/order-intent gates); [create-account-snapshot-manager.js](../../apps/harvester/src/bootstrap/account/create-account-snapshot-manager.js) (authoritative account/open-order snapshot); [subscribe-to-user-data.js](../../apps/harvester/src/bootstrap/user-data/subscribe-to-user-data.js) (updates/reconnect). Inspect current tests before adding coverage.

**Steps:**

1. [ ] **RED — Reproduce conflict:** unowned open BUY/SELL on symbol A, no owned order in OrderRegistry, otherwise-valid strategy decision. Assert no competing strategy order. Control: symbol B remains eligible.
2. [ ] **GREEN — Add narrow symbol gate:** use a current authoritative account-wide open-order view; defer only the affected symbol while a conflicting unowned order is open. Never adopt, cancel, modify or claim ownership of it.
3. [ ] **RED/GREEN — Snapshot lifecycle:** startup snapshot, order update/terminal event, reconnect refresh, stale/missing snapshot and snapshot-read failure. Unknown/stale state must not mean “no open orders”.
4. [ ] **Regression — Isolation/diagnostics:** no duplicate intent; external order unchanged; unrelated symbols unaffected; actionable blocked-symbol reason.

**Acceptance:** no conflicting same-symbol order can be submitted while an unowned order is open; external orders stay untouched/unowned; unrelated symbols remain independent; inability to establish current open-order state fails closed for that decision.

**Session evidence (2026-11-12/13):** PREFLIGHT found four unowned WLDFDUSD BUY orders. The LIVE strategy still submitted and filled WLDFDUSD orders while those external orders remained open; all four were later reported cancelled as unowned events. This is consistent with the runtime IGNORE policy but confirms P0.1 is not yet implemented. No external fills or balance mismatch were observed. See [session audit F-047](../../apps/harvester/docs/audits/sessions/AUDIT_SESSION_2026-11-12_19-27-13Z.md).

---

### P0.2 — Preserve exact commission facts and quote valuation through fill accounting

**Problem:** live commission validation supports third-asset commissions when historical quote valuation is supplied, but the lifecycle fill DTO drops `quoteValue` and the restore helper rejects third-asset commissions. The configured-market-only account snapshot filter can omit the commission asset. A fill accepted live must remain reconstructable and reconcilable. Missing valuation must never silently become a zero fee or be recomputed from today's price.

**Tracking:** [#654](https://github.com/45s/coinzilla/issues/654), forensic finding F-039. Keep live-accounting correction and durable-recovery integration as separate PRs if their contracts differ.

**Relevant code:** [position-accounting.js](../../apps/harvester/src/domain/portfolio/position-accounting.js) (Position cost/proceeds); [recovery-fill-accounting.js](../../apps/harvester/src/domain/strategies/conservative/recovery-fill-accounting.js); [lifecycle-event-dtos.js](../../apps/harvester/src/application/events/lifecycle-event-dtos.js) (safe DTO); [create-portfolio-workflow.js](../../apps/harvester/src/use-cases/create-portfolio-workflow.js) (live apply/restore); [create-account-snapshot-manager.js](../../apps/harvester/src/bootstrap/account/create-account-snapshot-manager.js) (fee-asset reconciliation).
